nodes.summary: A probability vector $m$ is a mean field equilibrium if and only if every state charged by $m$ minimises the cost: $m(x) \ne 0$ implies $F(x, m) \le F(y, m)$ for every $y$.
nodes.title: Equilibria are supported on minimisers

nodes.summary: A continuum of identical players each choose a state $y$ of a finite set $Q$; a player in state $y$ pays $F(y, m)$ when the population is distributed according to the probability vector $m$. A probability vector $m$ is a mean field equilibrium if that is $\int F(y, m)\, dm(y) = \inf_{m'} \int F(y, m)\, dm'(y)$: given the crowd, no player gains by deviating.
